subject: biology-2
question: A neuron fires at the start of its axon, and the signal travels all the way to the axon terminals without fading. Which statement best describes how the **all-or-none** action potential propagates along the axon?

options.text: The signal grows weaker with distance, like a ripple spreading across a pond.
Each segment fires at a smaller amplitude, so only short axons can transmit signals.
The signal stops at the first gap in the myelin sheath unless the stimulus is repeated.
The depolarization of one segment opens sodium channels in the next segment, so the full-strength signal regenerates at every point along the axon.

explanation: An action potential is all-or-none and regenerates, because the depolarization of one membrane region opens sodium channels in the adjacent region, so the impulse travels at full strength. A and B are false because action potentials do not weaken or shrink as they move along an axon. C is false because propagation is self-sustaining once the first action potential has fired.
